steps.title: Fundamentals analyst
steps.summary: AAPL's Q3 FY26 shows 16% sales growth, 50% gross margin, $101B nine-month net income, and net-cash balance sheet with $62B in buybacks. But the margin jump is partly tariff-refund accounting, and management explicitly warns intensifying component-cost inflation. steps.analysis: Q3 FY26 (June 27): revenue $109.4B (+16.4% y/y), products +18%, services +12%. Nine-month gross margin 49.0% vs 46.8%; Q3 products gross margin ~40.1% vs ~34.5% a year ago — an unusually large expansion. Mechanisms: (1) Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs in Feb 2026; Apple recognized refunds as reductions of products cost of sales, so part of the improvement is non-recurring; (2) services mix; (3) pricing. R&D is up 32% y/y ($34.0B nine months), consistent with the Siri AI/iOS 27 investment cycle flagged in MD&A, yet operating margin still expanded to 32.6%. Balance-sheet flags: inventories nearly doubled ($5.7B to $11.1B) — plausibly component pre-buying against the stated semiconductor/NAND/DRAM supply constraints, worth verifying; intangibles rose $9B. Debt reduced (commercial paper $8B to $2B, term repayments, no issuance) while buybacks continued from operating cash flow — financing activity is deleveraging plus capital return, not necessity. Macro context cuts both ways: fed funds 3.75-4.00% with the 10-year at 5.1% (largely real yield, 2.78% 10y TIPS) is a demanding discount-rate backdrop; credit spreads are tight (IG 105bp), so no funding stress. MD&A language — cost trends 'expected to intensify,' price increases may not fully mitigate — is a direct forward warning against extrapolating Q3 margin. Hypothesis to falsify: products margin expansion is mostly one-off refunds and will compress as Section 301 tariffs and memory costs bite in FY27.
